articles.title: ‘They used dogs’: New Al Jazeera film exposes Israel’s use of rape in jails
articles.summary: Former detainees detail systematic torture and sexual violence, including rape, while in Israeli custody.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains descriptions of sexual assault that some readers may find disturbing.

Muhammad al-Bakri specifically remembers the date of his rape.

It was April 10, 2024, during the Eid al-Fitr holiday, at the end of the holy month of Ramadan. The Gaza civil servant had been beaten, tortured, bound and forced to soil himself since his arrest by Israeli soldiers a month earlier.

The soldiers and their guard dogs surrounded him that day. “There were six soldiers on the right and six on the left,” he recalled. “They would ask your name. If you said ‘Muhammad’, they would say, ‘No, say your name is b****.’”

Al-Bakri said he was held with seven other prisoners. They were all stripped, blindfolded and handcuffed.

“We were raped after being stripped of our clothes,” he said. “We were shouting, ‘Oh Lord, oh God’, but they were just laughing and filming us.” Al-Bakri then echoed what several rights agencies have also reported – that guards also used dogs during the sexual abuse of prisoners. “The dogs were following commands from the officers to [attack] us,” he said.

“There was no mercy. We stayed in that state of sexual abuse and beatings for about 20 minutes to half an hour. Then they told us to get dressed and took us back to the prison.”

Al-Bakri is among multiple former prisoners who have given detailed testimonies to Al Jazeera for Bodies of Evidence: Israel’s Darkest Weapon, a documentary investigation into what International Criminal Court (ICC) judges, the United Nations and its special rapporteur on the occupied territories, Francesca Albanese, say amounts to the widespread and systematic use of rape and sexual torture by the Israeli army against Palestinians. Rights groups such as the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights (PCHR) and Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor have also documented testimonies of prisoners recounting how Israeli soldiers used dogs to rape them.

(Bodies of evidence: Israel’s Darkest Weapon)

Allegations of the sexual abuse of Palestinians in Israeli prisons are not new – they date back decades. But launching its genocidal war on Gaza following the Hamas-led attack of October 2023, Israel appears to have increased the use of rape as a weapon of war, according to the Al Jazeera investigation and various reports by the UN and leading rights groups.

A UN report published in March 2025 found evidence of the “systematic” use of sexual, reproductive and other forms of gender-based violence by Israel since October 7, 2023. In May, Israel was added to the UN “blacklist of sexual violence in conflict zones”. Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, Israeli rights group B’Tselem and the PCHR have described the pervasive culture of sexual violence within Israeli forces, especially among those charged with overseeing Palestinian prisoners. Many were arrested and held without charge under Israel’s system of administrative detention.

No soldiers or guards have been convicted of sexual abuse of Palestinians. Israel detained 10 security officers after a video of the rape of a prisoner was leaked from the Sde Teiman detention camp in the Negev desert in July 2024. But gangs of right-wing protesters, including legislators, attempted to storm the facility where the guards were being held in a bid to free them.

Last July, Israel dropped all charges against the guards. The female officer who allegedly leaked the video of the attack, Major-General Yifat Tomer-Yerushalmi, was subsequently arrested . Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu termed her “crime” – sharing footage of the rape by Israeli soldiers – as the “most severe public relations attack” on the country since its founding.

UN rapporteur Albanese said the intention behind the sexual abuse of Palestinian prisoners was clear: not simply to inflict pain, but to destroy the victim and their sense of self-worth.

“There is something deeper in the sense that torture, especially rape and other forms of sexual torture, destroys the mind of the person, especially in the capacity to rebuild or enjoy his or her intimacy,” she told Al Jazeera, recounting interviews with two survivors of rape.

Asked in the Knesset, Israel’s parliament, in July 2024 whether it was ever legitimate to rape a prisoner, Hanoch Milwidsky, a member of Netanyahu’s Likud party, shouted: “Yes.”

“If he is a Nukhba [Hamas fighter], everything is legitimate to do, everything.”

Casual labourer Job, which is how Al Jazeera has chosen to credit him, never thought there was anything particularly noteworthy about his life.

Like al-Bakri, Job thought he was an everyday middle-aged family man from Gaza. Both placed their children’s future above their own. Both prioritised their families’ safety since Israel launched its genocidal war in October 2023. Both had become accustomed to shepherding their families through the checkpoints, bombings and forced displacements that defined daily life in the besieged enclave.

That changed when both were taken prisoner, tortured and repeatedly raped by Israeli soldiers and guard dogs.

As with al-Bakri, Job’s memory of his rape is equally clear. “Female soldiers entered my room,” he told Al Jazeera. “They put iron handcuffs on my hands behind me. They untied the handcuffs from my legs and put on more handcuffs. Then they stripped me of my clothes.”

He was pinned to the ground with boots on his back and neck, while the female soldiers raped him using artificial objects.

“The soldiers around them were applauding and filming the scene. They were filming the rape scene.”

Job’s rape and sexual torture continued, all while being questioned for any knowledge of the Hamas-led attack of which he knew nothing.

The attack of October 7, 2023, during which 1,139 people were killed and about 250 abducted, ruptured much of Israeli society and assumptions about the relationship with Palestinians in the occupied territory.

Through endless loops on rolling news, the trauma of the attacks echoed throughout Israeli society, as the political class sought to amplify the harm inflicted upon Israel that day.

Recalling the events of his capture, Job recalled being blindfolded, tortured, trampled upon and beaten, all the while being questioned on the events of October 7, despite having no connection to what unfolded that day.

“They were telling us: ‘You know God and the Quranic verse, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. As you sow, so shall you reap,’” he recalled. Israeli soldiers told him: “You entered our lands, the Israeli lands, and invaded them. You raped and you did this and you did that”.

Al-Bakri was given a number for a name and described being beaten when he attempted to identify himself in any other way. “You are here as a prisoner of war,” he recalled being told. “You came here because of the destruction you caused.”

In addition to rape, al-Bakri said, he and other prisoners were attacked with dogs, and what he described as sound bombs intended to cause disorientation.

“You had to sleep on your stomach, hands tied and eyes blindfolded, while they walked dogs over you and kicked you,” he said.

Albanese told Al Jazeera that similar accounts of mistreatment and torture in the wake of the October 7 attack are common. “Brutality has escalated to an unprecedented level,” she said. “It became vindictive.”

“Regular practices have been severe beating, slapping, burning, broken bones, broken teeth, sexual violence, and rape,” she said. “Sexual penetration through objects, both bodily and other objects, like something that is recurrent, is the use of metal rods, cutting metal that might be knives, metal detectors, bottles.”

Many of the Israeli soldiers accused of taking part in the torture, sexual abuse and rape of Palestinian prisoners were raised in societies described by observers within Israel as having been conditioned to see Palestinians as somehow undeserving of human respect.

Organisations such as B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights Israel have described how many Israelis spend their entire lives without ever encountering Palestinians, a people destined by state policy to attend separate education systems.

Notions of Palestinians as being somehow outside the category of a recognisable people run deep in Israeli political culture, said sociologist Yehouda Shenhav-Shahrabani. That reaches back from the present to even the British Mandate for Palestine, when officials described it as a “land without a people” to the present, where they can be killed, raped and tortured with apparent impunity.

“By depicting the entire population as human animals and terrorists, and invoking the notion of human shields to justify massacres, Israel has effectively painted a target on the back of an entire civilian population as such,” Albanese told Al Jazeera. “Even children portrayed as terrorists in the making describe an overwhelming fear of imminent death.”

Israeli President Isaac Herzog had no issue with “unequivocally” blaming all Palestinians for the Hamas-led attack on October 7, telling reporters: “It is an entire nation out there that is responsible. It’s not true [that] this rhetoric about civilians not [being] aware, not involved. It’s absolutely not true.”

In the wake of the attack, former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant said Israel was fighting what he called “human animals” and ordered a “complete siege” on the men, women and children there. Others, such as Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, have been consistent offenders, routinely referring to Palestinians as terrorists or framing large segments of Palestinian society in broadly criminal or extremist terms, particularly in relation to Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

“Dehumanising language plays a key role in enterprises like a genocide or other forms of collective punishment and abuse,” Albanese said, “because, in order to treat the other as a subhuman, you need to see him or her as a subhuman.”

Despite what analysts have described as an established pattern of rape and sexual abuse against Palestinians, Israel has yet to receive legal censure from any multinational body or face sanctions for its actions in Gaza or the occupied West Bank. Attempts by international bodies, including the UN’s bid to investigate the allegations of sexual abuse in January 2025, were actively blocked by Israel.

Specific abuses – from forced nudity and threats of rape to assaults targeting genitals – have become standard practice for the Israeli forces, the UN has found, carried out with explicit or implicit approval from senior officials. Ben-Gvir, for instance, has decried investigations into the rape at Sde Teiman as “shameful”, while Defence Minister Israel Katz has described attempts to hold soldiers accountable for rape as a “blood libel”.

The torture of Palestinians has been glorified in Israel, Albanese remarked. “You have had not only Israeli officials and leaders boasting about how badly Palestinians were treated … Settlers and citizens alike have been taken to detention centres to observe, to watch, or to even [take part] in the humiliation inflicted on Palestinians.”

Triestino Mariniello, a professor at Liverpool John Moores University and part of the legal team representing Gaza’s victims at the ICC, pointed out what he described as a “very important difference under international criminal law between isolated acts of sexual violence and acts that are part of a systematic pattern against civilians”.

“The former may constitute war crimes. When the same acts are organised and widespread, they amount to crimes against humanity,” he said.

“These crimes take place in state detention centres and military detention centres. The fact that perpetrators are not tried, prosecuted, or convicted shows an institutional policy behind their commission,” Mariniello added.

To be sure, Palestinians continue to resist, Albanese said. “The Palestinians are still fighting not to be erased, not to be made extinct as a people with a capacity to determine themselves.”

But in the eyes of most observers, Israel’s genocide in Gaza is continuing in defiance of the paper ceasefire imposed upon Israel by United States President Donald Trump in October 2025 . Israel is pursuing the forcible displacement of Palestinians across the occupied West Bank at a rapid pace, with any resistance from the landowners and farmers to Israeli settlers and security forces typically met with violence, imprisonment, and often torture and rape.

“Surviving sexual violence and torture in general, and rape is brutal,” Albanese said. “Imagine when it’s done on a large-scale systemically to a population. It means to destroy the people as such.”

articles.title: Why GTA 6 actors may stay silent until release day despite growing cast speculation
articles.summary: Esports News: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans may have to wait until the game launches to learn who is behind its biggest characters. Rockstar Games has reportedly reminded.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans may have to wait until the game launches to learn who is behind its biggest characters. Rockstar Games has reportedly reminded actors who worked on GTA 6 that their non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) remain active until the game’s release on November 19. The reported warning comes as fans continue to guess the game’s cast from resumes, voice clips, and small hints. Rockstar has not officially confirmed the reported email, but the message could explain why many actors have stayed quiet about their roles.GTA 6 actors reportedly told to stay silent until November 19According to a report shared by GTA VI O’Clock, Rockstar reportedly sent an email reminding people who worked on the game about their NDAs. The message allegedly said that the date when they can announce their involvement is still November 19.The report claims the warning may have been sent to everyone who worked on GTA 6 in a performance role. This could include actors involved in voice acting, motion capture, or other performance work, rather than only the main stars.The reported email comes after actor Stephen Root became the first known GTA 6 actor to publicly confirm his role. Root told the Associated Press that he plays Brian Heder in the game.Root also explained why he believed his role became known. He said that too many people already knew him from King of the Hill and could recognize his voice. His comments gave fans one of their first clear pieces of information about the GTA 6 cast.Rockstar reportedly keeps GTA 6 cast mystery aliveRockstar has always kept GTA 6 details very secret. So far, fans have had to work out the possible cast using actor resumes, voice comparisons, and other clues instead of official announcements.The reported NDA reminder could mean fans will not get a big cast reveal before launch. Rockstar may also avoid introducing its actors through trailers, magazines, or other official promotions before November 19.Two names that continue to appear in fan discussions are Manni L. Perez and Dylan Rourke. Perez has been widely linked to Lucia, while Rourke has been connected to Jason. However, neither casting has been officially confirmed by Rockstar, and Perez has previously denied being involved.For now, Rockstar has not publicly commented on the reported email. That means the full cast remains a mystery.If the reported NDA reminder is real, GTA 6 actors may have to keep their roles secret until the game arrives on November 19. Stephen Root’s confirmation has already given fans one confirmed name, but Rockstar still appears to be keeping the rest of the cast hidden. articles.title: Driver charged over fatal A61 Barnsley crash that killed six people
articles.summary: Four members of the same family and a married couple on a motorbike died in the 2024 collision.
articles.body:
A man has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving over a crash that killed six people, including two children.

Shannen Morgan and Shane Roller died along with two of their daughters, nine-year-old Rubie, and Lillie, four, when the family's car collided with a motorbike on the A61 between Barnsley and Wakefield on 21 July 2024.

Husband and wife Christopher and Janine Barton, from Barnsley, who were both travelling on the motorcycle, also died in the crash.

Christopher Cockell, 50, is due to appear at Leeds Magistrates' Court in October charged with six counts of causing death by dangerous driving.

An inquest previously heard that the silver Ford Focus being driven by Mr Roller, 33, collided head on with the BMW motorcycle being driven by Mr Barton, 56, at about 15:50 BST between Staincross and Newmillerdam.

Wakefield Coroner's Court heard the collision happened as the motorcycle was overtaking another vehicle on the single-carriageway road, which had a 50mph (80 km/h) speed limit.

Coroner's support officer Phil Marr told the hearing: "As a result of a head-on impact, the car was spun to the side of the road, where it caught fire.

"It was not possible to release any of the occupants and all four were pronounced dead by paramedics at the scene."

Marr said a pathologist concluded Mr Barton's provisional cause of death was due to head and chest injuries.

He said Mrs Barton was "thrown onto the adjacent golf course" in the collision, with her death due to chest injuries.

Ms Morgan and van driver Mr Roller, who lived in Athersley, Barnsley, had another daughter, aged 11, who was not with them at the time of the crash.

An online fundraising page, set up by a family friend in the wake of the tragedy, raised more than £400,000 for her.

In a social media post at the time, Mr Roller's father, Graham, paid tribute to the couple, who he described as an "amazing" mum and dad.

"Shane wasn't just a son but an amazing father and he had a heart of gold," he wrote.

"Shannen, our daughter-in-law, was funny and was also an amazing mum and they thought the world of their little family."

Co-head teachers of Athersley North Primary School, which Rubie and Lillie had attended, said the girls had been "a delight to teach".

In a statement, Clare Storr and Kirsty Wordsworth, said: "The girls were a credit to their parents, who were always incredibly supportive and who will also be greatly missed."

Mr and Mrs Barton, 48, who had lived in Barnsley, had recently celebrated their 25th wedding anniversary.

In a tribute issued via West Yorkshire Police in 2024, their son described his parents as "a loving, caring mum and dad who always put me before everything else".

A spokesperson for West Yorkshire Police said Cockell had been summoned following an investigation by the force's Major Collision Enquiry Team and would appear before magistrates on 28 October.

Cockell, of Gresford Close, Woolley Grange, had already been facing a charge of failing to stop at the scene of a collision.

articles.title: 49ers face logjam on injured reserve with Demarcus Robinson out 3-6 weeks
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson and DT James Thompson Jr. have high ankle sprains that could cost them a month and a half, but the crowd of players...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers look like a legitimate contender through two weeks. At the same time, the team already has so many injuries that it is considering keeping players with multi-week ailments on the active roster, rather than placing them on the injured reserve list.

NFL teams can place an unlimited number of players on IR during a given season. Players must miss a minimum of four games once put on IR. But only eight of them can be designated to return. Thus, as wide receiver Demarcus Robinson and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. grapple with high ankle sprains that could keep them on the shelf for 3-6 weeks, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan, the 49ers may hold both players on the active roster so as to not cut into those eight spots.

"Those guys (Robinson and Thompson) are right in that area … of how long those take (to recover from)," Shanahan said. "(But) it's real early for us to have as many (injuries) as we've had, so we got to balance all that out."

Robinson caught three passes for 34 yards before he was carted to the locker room early in the 49ers' 35-13 shellacking of the Miami Dolphins on Sunday at Levi's Stadium. Robinson had worked his way into the No. 3 receiver role for San Francisco following injuries to Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling .

"Yeah, it sucks," quarterback Brock Purdy said postgame of Robinson's injury. "These are all extremely great playmakers that, looking at our roster in OTAs and camp, it's like, 'Oh shoot, we can do some damage.' And then Ricky goes down, Stribling, and now D-Rob. … for them to go down early in the season like that is tough."

In the meantime, Shanahan said fellow wide receivers Jacob Cowing , Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge will have increased roles, while the 49ers' front office is "working on all possibilities, looking at everything that's out there" for possible outside reinforcements.

Also worth noting: Shanahan said the 49ers will have to manage the workload of wide receiver Mike Evans - who left Sunday's game with a hip injury - throughout practices this week. But it doesn't sound like his hip is a major concern at the moment.

As for the defensive line, Thompson's injury further damages the 49ers' interior depth, as it follows the season-ending injury to second-year defensive tackle Alfred Collins . Thompson, an undrafted rookie, rotated in for 19 snaps Sunday prior to getting hurt. The healthy defensive tackles on the 49ers' active roster are Osa Odighizuwa , Gracen Halton and CJ West. Halton, another rookie, had a standout performance Sunday and has already earned an increased role in defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' system.

San Francisco has the following players on IR who could be designated to return at some point: Stribling, WR Christian Kirk , OL Austen Pleasants, CB Nate Hobbs , LB Nick Martin and DL Sam Okuayinonu . It's unlikely all those players will be back on the active roster this year, but the first three are the most obvious candidates. Kirk is eligible to return to practice after the 49ers' Oct. 4 matchup against the Denver Broncos .

articles.title: Major US outlets boycott shared Trump coverage in protest at media ban
articles.summary: Regular coverage of the president has been disrupted after he banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.
articles.body:
Major US television networks suspended their pooled coverage of President Donald Trump on Monday in response to CNN, Politico and MS NOW being barred from the White House.

Trump announced the ban on Friday as he accused the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday.

The three US outlets have since said they will sue the Trump administration in a bid to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".

Shortly after, the White House launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, which operates a 24/7 feed of clips of the president.

Several other US outlets have also announced that they would not participate in coverage of pooled events, with some, including the New York Times and Washington Post, saying they would not share still images from Trump events on Monday.

It meant there was no network TV footage of Trump boarding Air Force One or arriving in New York to attend the UN general assembly.

Trump also took part in a ribbon-cutting ceremony for the new Marine One helipad on the White House South Lawn. The event was streamed on the White House site but his comments were inaudible.

The president did later appear on television following a meeting with the Mayor of New York Zohran Mamdani. He told the president that all members of the media would be welcome at the press conference.

Trump said: "It's interesting because, they said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me, so I wasn't very worried about that. Look at all that press."

The pool involves media organisations sharing material to save on costs and space when broadcasting presidential events to the American public.

Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, who currently holds a rotating role helping to organise media TV crews covering the White House, wrote in an email seen by the BBC that "effective today, the TV pool will not be covering designated as pool coverage" of Trump.

The message said the move followed the White House "preventing" CNN from fulfilling its pool duties for Trump's trip to New York and that "there will be no replacement pool put in place".

The three media organisations banned from the White House filed a lawsuit on Monday in US District Court in Washington.

A joint statement announcing the legal action said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.

"Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."

articles.title: Chargers Snag Former Jaguars Weapon Amid Injuries to Tight Ends
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers placed tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar on injured reserve (IR) after the pair both suffered injuries in the Week 2 loss to...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers placed tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar on injured reserve (IR) after the pair both suffered injuries in the Week 2 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders .

According to ESPN's Kris Rhim, the Bolts have signed former Jacksonville Jaguars TE Hayden Rucci off their practice squad.

"The Chargers signed tight end Hayden Rucci to the active roster from Jacksonville's practice squad. Rucci has familiarity with Mike McDaniel, played four games in Miami last season. He's never caught a pass in the NFL . [The Chargers] waived WR Gary Jennings in a corresponding move."

Njoku and Kolar were both free agent additions this offseason to help the offense thrive under McDaniel, but won't have much impact due to their injuries.

Rucci last played for the Miami Dolphins in the 2025 season, logging just one tackle. The tight end also played snaps on special teams.

Before adding Rucci to the active roster, second-year tight end Oronde Gadsden was the only healthy tight end.

To make room for Hayden Rucci, the Los Angeles Chargers have waived wide receiver Gary Jennings .

The WR played one game for the Bolts, in Week 2 and mainly on special teams, before parting ways with the player to make space for a depleted tight end room.

Jennings is a former fourth-round selection from the 2019 class and has yet to record a catch himself. The WR has played in just two games in his career, with the other being for the Miami Dolphins .

Now, the former West Virginia Mountaineer will have to find a new home. Gary Jennings has been part of nine different NFL teams and has spent some time in the United Football League.

For the first time in his coaching career, collegiate or professional, Jim Harbaugh is off to a 0-2 start to a season.

Now looking to get back on the win column, the head coach said he has seen positives from his team, according to Kris Rhim.

"I do. And I see improvement and I think I said it last night after the game, just the competitive endurance, the overcoming adversity, some warriors out there and we continue to build."

"I thought our team had a real sense of urgency. I thought the effort, the overcoming the adversity, several things."

While Harbaugh originally appeared to sidestep the question, the head coach has some knowledge of how his team enters Week 3.

While adding Hayden Rucci is a small step, it is pivotal to prevent the team from being without a tight end on the active roster.

The Bolts look to get their first win of the season against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

articles.title: Yemen government forces claim control of Mount Qarfan in Taiz
articles.summary: Major General Abdulaziz al-Majidi says five Houthi fighters killed and 20 wounded after ‘fierce battles’.
articles.body:
Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces say they have taken full control of strategic Mount Qarfan in the western governorate of Taiz during a battle with Iran-aligned Houthi fighters.

Government forces, assisted by local fighters, secured Mount Qarfan on Tuesday, the Yemen Armed Forces Media Center said in a statement, as the warring sides battle for control of highlands overlooking the Red Sea coast.

The chief of staff for the Taiz military axis, Major General Abdulaziz al-Majidi, said troops engaged in “fierce battles” with Houthi rebels, killing five Houthi fighters, wounding 20 and achieving the “restoration of control” of the mountain.

The seizure of Mount Qarfan would give Yemen’s government forces commanding fire control and surveillance over the surrounding valleys between the ash-Shamaytaun and al-Waziiya districts in southern Taiz governorate.

There was no immediate comment from the Houthis on the government forces’ claim.

The clashes come as fighting continues to rage in Yemen amid mounting regional tensions set off by the United States-Israel war on Iran.

The Houthis, who seized Yemen’s Red Sea coast this month, including the port of Mocha, have launched an attempt to push into the Kahboub Mountains in Taiz and Lahj governorates. Control of the strategic heights, which overlook the Bab al-Mandeb strait and Mayyun Island in the Red Sea, would allow the Houthis to sever the coast from the remaining government-held south.

Analysts told Al Jazeera that the Houthis were likely seeking to gain control of the mountains to provide a defensive shield for the group’s forces on the coast.

“The mountains are the natural wall that protects the Houthis’ rear on the coast. Controlling them would cut the coast off from the government-held south and place direct pressure on Lahj and, in the longer term, Aden,” Faozi Al-Goidi, a visiting fellow at the Middle East Council on Global Affairs, told Al Jazeera.

The battles for the highlands near the Red Sea coast come as fighting continues across Yemen.

Yahya Saree, a Houthi military spokesperson, said on Tuesday that Houthi forces shot down a reconnaissance drone over Mocha in Taiz governorate.

He also said Saudi warplanes carried out 19 air strikes over the past day, hitting targets in Taiz, al-Jawf and Marib governorates.

The government-aligned Yemeni News Agency reported that Houthi forces also shelled residential neighbourhoods in central Taiz city, causing damage to homes.

The World Health Organization said 674 people had been killed and almost 3,000 injured in renewed fighting since August 6, including 164 deaths and 516 injuries on September 13-18 alone.

Meanwhile, civilians continue to be forced from their homes during a growing displacement crisis.

More than 158,000 people have been displaced this month, according to Yemen’s Executive Unit for the Management of Displaced Persons Camps.

Ibrahim Al-Huri, an assistant professor at the University of Saba Region, told Al Jazeera that civilians are paying “the highest prices” in the war.

“Three thousand people have crossed the sea to Djibouti and Somalia to seek refuge and safety, using primitive boats, putting their lives at risk,” he said.

“People have become desperate,” he added. “They have lost their homes, their farms, their sources of income, and many of them have fled to overcrowded camps where people are already in a struggle to access food, sanitation, water and medical facilities.”

articles.title: Multas ônibus Campinas: Emdec aplica 36 mil e 40% não são pagas | G1
articles.standfirst: Infrações geraram R$ 18,8 milhões de janeiro a julho de 2026, mas apenas R$ 11,1 milhões foram arrecadados. Órgão afirma que recurso é investido na manutenção de terminais e fiscalização.
articles.summary: Multas ônibus Campinas somam R$ 18,8 milhões em 2026, mas falta de pagamento das empresas afeta a manutenção de terminais e a fiscalização do transporte público.
articles.body:
Ônibus do transporte público municipal de Campinas — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

A Empresa Municipal de Desenvolvimento de Campinas (Emdec) aplicou 36.657 multas às concessionárias e cooperativas do transporte público da cidade entre janeiro e julho de 2026. O número de autuações representa uma alta de 47% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado , quando foram registradas 24.916 infrações .

O volume de infrações gerou um total de R$ 18,8 milhões em penalidades , mas 40,7% desse montante ainda não foi pago pelas operadoras do sistema . Na prática, os R$ 7,6 milhões que deixaram de entrar nos cofres públicos neste ano equivalem a quase todo o valor que foi efetivamente arrecadado pela Emdec em 2025.

"Todo auto de infração gerado, ele tem a possibilidade de quem está sofrendo o auto de infração entrar com recurso. E aí esse alto de infração muitas vezes pode decorrer de meses para que ele seja julgado. Se ele for julgado como a empresa perdeu, aí ela é descontado isso do subsídio repassado aos mesmos", explica Claudio Fernandes, gerente de fiscalização da Emdec.

Os dados foram obtidos via Lei de Acesso à Informação (LAI) pela EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo.

A Emdec informou que os valores efetivamente arrecadados com as multas são aplicados integralmente no custeio de atividades da gestão e operação do transporte coletivo.

Com o aumento das autuações, o montante arrecadado subiu de R$ 8 milhões em 2025 para R$ 11,1 milhões em 2026 . A maior parte da verba paga pelas operadoras neste ano foi destinada para:

Terminais e estações: R$ 4,1 milhões (37,3%) foram usados para zeladoria, segurança 24 horas, limpeza e manutenção das estruturas físicas e abrigos.

Fiscalização e operação: R$ 2,2 milhões (20%) mantiveram as equipes que verificam as frotas e o cumprimento dos horários nas ruas.

Outras áreas: O restante financiou setores de administração e jurídico (18,5%), planejamento (11,6%), monitoramento e controle operacional (7,3%), além de tecnologia e comunicação.

Abrigo de ponto de ônibus quebrado em Campinas — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Apesar dos recursos destinados à manutenção do sistema, passageiros que utilizam o transporte público diariamente relatam problemas frequentes na estrutura oferecida nas ruas. A situação afeta diretamente quem aguarda pelos veículos nos bairros, contrastando com os investimentos apresentados na planilha oficial.

Em um ponto de parada localizado na Avenida Jorge Tibiriçá, por exemplo, a cobertura apresenta danos no teto e há placas soltas. Já na Rua Major Luciano Teixeira, no bairro Bonfim, um local de desembarque com grande fluxo de estudantes e idosos não possui piso concretado, obrigando os usuários a pisarem em terra, lama e entulhos espalhados.

Além das falhas estruturais nos pontos, os usuários do sistema também enfrentam dificuldades com a frota em circulação. As principais reclamações diárias envolvem atrasos constantes, sumiço de veículos nos aplicativos de monitoramento, falta de ar-condicionado, janelas quebradas e ônibus que apresentam falhas mecânicas durante as viagens.

Segundo a Emdec, no caso do abrigo da Avenida Jorge Tibiriçá, os reparos na cobertura estão programados para sexta-feira (25). Já na Major Luciano Teixeira, uma vistoria para avaliar as condições da estrutura existente está prevista para esta quinta. Pelo local circula a linha 271, Jardim Pacaembu.

A Emdec explicou ainda que nem todos os pontos de parada têm as condições necessárias para receber cobertura. Para definir onde os abrigos podem ser instalados, são levados em conta critérios como a demanda de embarque, o número de passageiros e de linhas que atendem ao local, além da proximidade de escolas e postos de saúde.

Sobre a linha 264, Vila Padre Anchieta, a empresa informou que vai reforçar a fiscalização. Em relação aos problemas na estrutura interna dos ônibus, as denúncias devem informar o prefixo do veículo para que a vistoria possa ser realizada.

Os operadores das duas linhas serão acionados para identificar e corrigir as situações relatadas. Pedidos de melhorias na infraestrutura de transporte e mobilidade podem ser feitos pelo telefone 118 ou pelo WhatsApp, no número (19) 3731-2910 .

articles.title: Hawaii under another hurricane watch as new storm closes in
articles.summary: Nolo is expected to become a hurricane sometime Thursday night and could become a major hurricane by the weekend as it approaches Hawaii's Big Island.
articles.body:
Hawaii's Big Island was under a hurricane watch late Wednesday night after Tropical Storm Nolo formed in the Pacific Ocean earlier in the day, the National Hurricane Center said.

Nolo is expected to become a hurricane by Thursday night and could become a major hurricane by the weekend, the center said. A storm is considered a major hurricane when it reaches Category 3 or higher on the hurricane scale , meaning it has maximum sustained winds of at least 111 mph.

Storm Nolo had maximum sustained winds of 50 mph as of late Wednesday night local time. Its core was some 460 miles south-southeast of Honolulu and 285 miles south of South Point, which is on the Big Island.

Nolo was crawling north at 2 mph, but a "general north to north-northeast motion is expected through Friday, followed by a sharp westward turn by Saturday in the vicinity of the Big Island," the Miami-based hurricane center said.

Nolo is expected to approach the Big Island on Friday and Saturday.

The storm is expected to bring around 15 to 20 inches of rain to the Big Island, with up to 35 inches possible in some areas. The heavy rain could trigger "catastrophic life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the hurricane center warned.

Maui could see 5 to 10 inches of rain, with totals of up to 20 inches in some areas. Maui could also see life-threatening flooding and mudslides. The rest of the islands were forecast to get about 1 to 3 inches with 6 inches at most and could see isolated flooding.

Nolo formed as another storm, Hurricane Polo , continued to swirl in the Pacific, off Mexico's southwestern coast.

The latest storms add to an unsually active season in the Pacific. Earlier this month, Hurricane Lowell brought damaging winds and heavy rain to the western Hawaiian islands of Kauai and Niihau, bringing down trees, damaging roads and knocking out power for thousands.

Last month, Hurricane Lala washed away about 100 homes , triggered landslides and caused widespread power outages as it brushed past Hawaii.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says shot down 6 ballistic missiles launched by Houthis
articles.summary: No response by Yemen’s Houthis to a claim by the coalition forces that its missiles targeted Taif and Yanbu.
articles.body:
Saudi-led coalition forces fighting Yemen’s Houthis say they have intercepted six ballistic missiles allegedly fired by the Iran-allied group towards cities in Saudi Arabia.

The missiles were destroyed on Thursday in the direction of the Saudi cities of Taif and the strategically important port of Yanbu, according to Major General Turki al-Malki, the spokesman for the Saudi-backed Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen.

Saudi air defences intercepted some of the missiles attempting to target the cities, Al-Malki told the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

There was no immediate claim of responsibility from the Houthis or other groups.

The coalition statement came as the Reuters news agency reported that an ‌‌air defence system operated by Greek ⁠⁠military ⁠⁠personnel in Saudi Arabia intercepted a ballistic missile and a drone on Thursday in ⁠⁠the wider Yanbu region, home to major oil refining facilities.

“Both were shot down,” a Greek security source told Reuters, adding that the Greek Patriot system launched two missiles but did not give details ⁠⁠on the origin of the ⁠⁠drone and the ballistic missile. A second source confirmed the information to the news agency.

Yanbu port is key to Saudi crude when shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are disrupted.

Earlier on Thursday, Saudi Arabia’s General Directorate of Civil Defence issued alerts warning of potential danger in the holy city of Mecca, the northwestern area of Tabuk, the Red Sea areas of Jeddah and Yanbu and the southern area of Taif. They later said the threat had passed and the cities were out of danger.

Last week, Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a drone launched by the Houthis towards Mecca , an accusation the group strongly denied, with Houthi leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi calling the Saudi claims “a heinous lie”.

It was the first time in nearly 10 years that a security alert had been activated in Mecca, home to the Kaaba, Islam’s holiest site.

The Houthis have largely attacked southern areas of Saudi Arabia.

They stepped up attacks on the kingdom after declaring a naval blockade in July, a second theatre for the US-Iran war. The Houthis also seized the whole of Yemen’s western coast in a lightning offensive nearly two weeks ago that brought them to the shores of the Red Sea’s strategic Bab al-Mandeb waterway.

Forces with Yemen’s Saudi-backed internationally recognised government said on Thursday they repelled Houthi attacks along several fronts in Yemen’s southwestern Taiz governorate.

Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili, spokesman for the Yemeni government forces, said that the Houthis launched coordinated attacks on Wednesday night in a bid to reach positions on a key road connecting the Aden, Lahj and Taiz governorates.

articles.body: Rockstar Games has officially announced the GTA 6 Collector’s Edition, titled “Grand Theft Auto 6: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection.” The special edition is packed with more than a dozen physical items themed around Vice City and Leonida, and it's now available to pre-order.The fans are pretty excited about the Collector’s Edition, and it is perfect for those who want to get their hands on themed merchandise related to the game. articles.title: Embraer entrega 1º avião C-390 Millennium à Força Aérea do Uzbequistão | G1
articles.standfirst: Aeronave é produzida em Gavião Peixoto (SP), onde ocorreu evento de entrega nesta sexta-feira (25). Uzbequistão se torna o primeiro operador do C-390 Millennium na Ásia Central.
articles.summary: Aeronave é produzida em Gavião Peixoto (SP). Uzbequistão se torna o primeiro operador do C-390 Millennium na Ásia Central
articles.body:
C-390 Millennium é entregue à Força Aérea do Uzbequistão em Gavião Peixoto (SP) — Foto: Embraer/Divulgação

A Embraer entregou nesta sexta-feira (25) a primeira aeronave de transporte multimissão C-390 Millennium à Força Aérea do Uzbequistão durante uma cerimônia realizada nas instalações da Embraer em Gavião Peixoto (SP).

A entrega contou com a presença do Major-General Akhmad Jamolovich Burkhonov, Comandante da Força Aérea, e Olimkhon Bakiyevich Rustamov, diretor da empresa estatal "O‘ztextreyd", representando a República do Uzbequistão.

O contrato, assinado no final de 2024, também inclui um pacote de treinamento e suporte, além do fornecimento de peças de reposição.

O Uzbequistão se torna o primeiro operador do C-390 Millennium na Ásia Central, assinalando um marco importante nos esforços do país para modernizar e fortalecer capacidades de mobilidade aérea.

"A entrega do primeiro C-390 Millennium representa um passo significativo para a modernização da Força Aérea do Uzbequistão. O desempenho excepcional, a versatilidade e as capacidades multimissão da aeronave nos permitirão executar uma ampla gama de missões com maior eficiência e prontidão. Estamos ansiosos para introduzir esta plataforma de última geração em serviço e fortalecer ainda mais nossas capacidades operacionais", disse o Major-General Akhmad Jamolovich Burkhonov, Comandante da Força Aérea do Uzbequistão.

"Estamos honrados em entregar o primeiro C-390 Millennium à Força Aérea do Uzbequistão e dar as boas-vindas ao Uzbequistão à crescente comunidade de operadores do C-390 no mundo todo", disse Bosco da Costa Júnior, Presidente e CEO da Embraer Defesa & Segurança.

"A escolha do C-390 confirma seu status como a solução de mobilidade aérea mais avançada disponível atualmente. Essa entrega reforça nosso compromisso de apoiar o Uzbequistão com capacidade incomparável e flexibilidade operacional para as próximas décadas."

Com essa primeira entrega, o Uzbequistão se junta a um grupo crescente de nações que operam o C-390 Millennium, reforçando a posição da aeronave como o novo padrão no transporte aéreo tático de médio porte.

Avião C-390 Millennium é entregue à Força Aérea do Uzbequistão em Gavião Peixoto (SP) — Foto: Embraer/Divulgação

O C-390 Millennium, construído e projetado no século 21, é a aeronave de transporte militar mais moderna de sua categoria.

Ele pode transportar mais carga útil (26 toneladas) do que outras aeronaves militares de transporte de médio porte, voando mais rápido (470 nós) e mais longe.

É capaz de executar uma ampla gama de missões, incluindo transporte de carga e tropas, lançamentos de equipamentos e pessoal, evacuação médica, busca e salvamento (SAR), combate a incêndios e missões humanitárias, operando a partir de pistas temporárias ou não pavimentadas.

Quando equipado com sistema de reabastecimento aéreo (AAR) de instalação rápida, pode atuar tanto como tanque, quanto como receptor.

Além da Força Aérea Brasileira, a aeronave multimissão de última geração foi selecionada pelas forças aéreas de Portugal, Hungria, República da Coreia, Holanda, Áustria, República Tcheca, República do Uzbequistão, Suécia, Emirados Árabes Unidos, Eslováquia, Colômbia e Lituânia.

O C-390 Millennium oferece capacidade, confiabilidade, versatilidade e desempenho incomparáveis para atender às necessidades táticas e estratégicas das forças aéreas em todo o mundo com interoperabilidade entre seus operadores.

Out: Linebacker Devin Lloyd , linebacker Claudin Cherelus , safety Nick Scott

Questionable: Wide receivers Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette

Now, the good news on Coker and Legette is they were both limited participants in Friday's practice. Here's to hoping both of the Panthers' young wide receivers can see the field on Sunday. But the three defensive players who are out for Sunday is going to make things very, very hard on that side of the ball. Losing Devin Lloyd, in particular, is a massive loss.

The Panthers have been active on the transactions front this week. Here are the most noteworthy moves.

Placed running back Jonathon Brooks on Injured Reserve

The injury-prone young running back just can't catch a break when it comes to his health. The 2024 second round pick will miss at least six weeks after having surgery to repair a core muscle. He has appeared in just five games over three seasons.

Signed safety Isaiah Simmons to the active roster from the practice squad

Originally the No. 8 overall pick in the 2020 draft, he spent his first three seasons with the Arizona Cardinals and racked up 258 tackles, 7.5 sacks, seven forced fumbles, and four interceptions. But Simmons was a "tweener" and when the Cardinals hired a new coaching staff, they didn't view him as a fit at either linebacker or safety. He was traded to the New York Giants in 2023 and had 71 tackles over two seasons as an occasional fill-in starter.

Last year he was signed to the Panthers practice squad then appeared in five games for Carolina in 2025 with two tackles. He played one defensive snap and 87 on special teams.

He continues to yo-yo between the Panthers practice squad and active roster this year. In 2026 he has appeared in both of Carolina's games, playing five defensive snaps and 49 on special teams.

Signed wide receiver Ihmir Smith-Marsette to the practice squad

Smith-Marsette's name probably rings a bell for some Panthers fans. He spent the 2023 season in Carolina and was the team's primary punt returner, averaging 8.7 yards per return and taking one to the house. He also contributed eight receptions for 51 yards plus eight carries for 74 yards and a touchdown.

Smith-Marsette was a fifth-round pick by the Vikings in 2021 and has bounced around several teams. In 2024 he was the Giants' punt returner and also returned 11 kickoffs, including taking one back for a touchdown. The Giants released him during final roster cuts in 2025 and he didn't latch on with any other team last year.

He gives the Panthers another potential option in the return game following the recent release of Jimmy Horn Jr.

Signed linebacker Maema Njongmeta to the practice squad

Njongmeta began his career in 2024 as an undrafted free agent with the Cincinnati Bengals and had 13 tackles and two fumble recoveries in 17 games, playing mostly special teams. Last year the Panthers claimed him off the Bengals' practice squad and he appeared in 15 games for Carolina in 2025 with 10 tackles as a special teams mainstay. This year he was waived at final roster cuts, but the Panthers have now added him back to the practice squad.

articles.title: Bucs’ Todd Bowles Confirms Two Key Defenders Are Out for Sunday
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were already facing a difficult Week 3 matchup. Now they will have to do it without two important pieces of their defense. Head coac...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were already facing a difficult Week 3 matchup. Now they will have to do it without two important pieces of their defense.

Head coach Todd Bowles confirmed that outside linebacker Rueben Bain Jr. and inside linebacker Josiah Trotter will both miss Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings . The news comes with the Buccaneers still searching for their first win of the season, making the timing especially tough.

Todd Bowles Loses Josiah Trotter And Rueben Bain Jr. For Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Trotter's absence stands out most. The rookie linebacker has quickly become one of the more productive defenders on the Bucs roster, and he has made an impact in both games to open his NFL career.

He came up with 11 tackles, a sack, and an interception return for a touchdown in the season opener against the Cincinnati Bengals . Trotter also played well against the Cleveland Browns in Week 2 before briefly leaving the game with a shoulder issue. He eventually returned; however, the injury remained something to watch during the week.

That concern became real when Bowles ruled him out, and Bain will be unable to play in the Vi kings game due to a groin injury. However, unlike Trotter, the first-round draft choice has not had as much statistical impact over the first two weeks of the season.

The Buccaneers will now turn to their linebacker depth. SirVocea Dennis and Christian Rozeboom are expected to see time at inside linebacker depending on the defensive package, while Alex Anzalone remains part of the group. The Bucs were already having trouble consistently getting off the field and making tackles. Losing Trotter removes a player who had quickly established himself as a reliable presence in the middle of the defense.

That could become particularly important against Minnesota. There are several Vikings players who have t he ability to cause problems on Sunday in open space, including Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison , T.J. Hockenson , and Aaron Jones . The latter could also be an interesting matchup for a Bucs defense that will play without its most productive young linebacker.

The young man has been the only one in the team having scored an interception within the first two games played, as well as a sack and the highest number of tackles within the team. They also can't afford another slow start. Tampa Bay is 0-2 after losses to Cincinnati and Cleveland, including a disappointing home defeat to the Browns in Week 2.

Bowles said Dennis and Rozeboom will both play at inside linebacker depending on the package. The coaching staff will have to find a way to spread Trotter's workload across the remaining defenders.

For a team still looking for its first win, losing two defensive contributors before a matchup with the Vikings makes an already important game even more difficult.

articles.title: Why 11-year-old Yuki Kurihara felt 'embarrassed' after winning Asian Games esports gold
articles.summary: At just 11 years old, Japan’s Yuki Kurihara has already won an Asian Games gold medal.
articles.body: At just 11 years old, Japan’s Yuki Kurihara has already won an Asian Games gold medal. But after beating players much older than him, the young esports player said he felt “embarrassed” and could not show much emotion.Kurihara, a primary school student and the youngest athlete in Japan’s Asian Games history, defeated South Korea’s 24-year-old Kang Dongshin 10-2 in the Puyo Puyo Champions final on Saturday.A gold medal after dominating older playersKurihara had an impressive run to the final. In the semi-final, he defeated Thailand’s Tanarak Wongkitkun, 28, by a huge 10-1 margin. The win guaranteed him at least a silver medal.The final was also one-sided, although Kurihara lost the opening game 1-0. He then took control and went on to win 10-2.Despite the victory, Kurihara did not celebrate wildly.“To be completely honest, I felt a bit embarrassed, so I couldn’t really show my expressions or change my face much,” he said.‘The gold medal is really beautiful’Kurihara looked calm throughout the competition. When he received his gold medal on the podium, he gave a slight bow before giving a small wave to the arena.“I’m really happy. The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy,” he said.“Also, the plush toy is super cute, and it’s cool that it is gold-coloured too.”Started playing Puyo Puyo in primary schoolKurihara began playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school. He soon started taking part in tournaments and winning them. He received his professional licence in April this year and has regularly beaten adult players.“It’s hard having to balance it with school and cram school, but it’s really fun,” Kurihara had said before the Asian Games.Puyo Puyo Champions is a puzzle game in which players clear coloured blobs from their screen by lining them up and making them disappear.Youngest at the Asian Games?There are no publicly available records showing the youngest medallists in Asian Games history. The Games were first held in 1951. Indonesia’s Bunga Nyimas won a bronze medal in women’s skateboarding at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games when she was 12.Three years ago, China’s Cui Chenxi won gold in the women’s street skateboarding event at the Hangzhou Asian Games at the age of 13.Kurihara, meanwhile, has now made his own mark at the Asian Games at just 11.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Four killed in helicopter crash near Montreal
articles.summary: The victims of the crash have not yet been identified, Quebec provincial police told the BBC.
articles.body:
Four people have died after a helicopter crashed in a small town 50km (31 miles) from Montreal, Quebec's provincial police have told the BBC.

Emergency services were called to Sainte-Brigide-d'Iberville shortly after 14:30 local time (19:30 BST) on Saturday afternoon, where they found the aircraft on fire and declared its occupants dead at the scene.

The victims have not yet been identified but the aircraft appeared to be a private helicopter, Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said.

An investigation into the crash is being led by the Major Crime Unit of the Sûreté du Québec, working alongside crime scene technicians as well as investigators from the Transportation Safety Board of Canada.

The crash site is located near the Rang des Écossais road off Highway 10, according to Bilodeau.

In an emergency call, police were notified of a helicopter in distress that may have crashed and caught fire.

An hour after the call, the fire at the site had been brought under control though officials were still working at the crash site just before 22:00 local time (03:00 GMT).

The victims have not yet been identified and Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said this process may "take a few days."

articles.title: Right Away, Red Wings May Not Need to Make Roster Moves
articles.summary: Todd McLellan didn’t want to be that guy, but the Detroit Red Wings coach couldn’t help himself. He thought back […]
articles.body:
Todd McLellan didn't want to be that guy, but the Detroit Red Wings coach couldn't help himself.

He thought back to a final roster selection when he was an NHL hopeful as a player, and suffered what at the time felt like the unkindest cut of all.

"I think back to when I played, and that's a really bad thing for a coach ever to say, but I remember having that camp, and I was bitter because I thought I had a really good camp," McLellan said. "But now that I look back on it, that other guy over there had a great camp, like a really good camp. And if I was picking the team, I would have picked it the way the management team did back then, too.

"I didn't like it because I thought I played as well as I could. So maybe we'll have some of those guys in that situation."

Or maybe they won't. At least not right away.

Here's the thing: If the Red Wings don't get resolutions in the next day with scenarios involving three players, the Detroit roster may already be set.

Forward Dylan Larkin (upper-body injury) and defenseman Jacob Bernard-Docker (upper-body injury) are hurt. If they aren't going to be ready for Friday's regular-season opener against the New York Rangers , they'll be placed on injured reserve.

Defenseman Simon Edvinsson is a restricted free agent who is still without a contract. Until he signs on the dotted line, he can't play.

Assuming those three aren't figuring in the mix, for the time being, Detroit's roster would be set. Minus Larkin, there are 13 forwards left. If Edvinsson and Bernard-Docker aren't in the mix, that leaves eight other defensemen.

Add in goalies John Gibson and Daniil Tarasov , and you've got your 23-player roster.

Englund Ready to Set Sail With The Red Wings

Perhaps the biggest surprise in all this deciphering is that no matter what, it appears that newly-acquired Andreas Englund will be staying with the Red Wings. The 6-foot-4, 200-pound journeyman NHL defenseman was claimed on waivers from the Calgary Flames on Saturday.

McLellan coached him with the Los Angeles Kings . He likes the elements that Englund can add to the roster.

"He will fit our room really well," McLellan said. "He's fit, he works hard at his game, he has played in the system that we're trying to put in, and he's physical, and he's tough, and he shepherds the group. So we like all those attributes that he'll bring in.

"When he's in the lineup, he'll give you everything he has, and when he's not in the lineup, he'll give you everything he can from the outside."

From the outside, there's a sense of finality when the opening-night roster is officially announced. In reality, the lineup is like the TV listings. It's always subject to change.

The roster must be submitted on Monday. But the Red Wings don't open the season until Friday. That's a large window of opportunity for change to occur.

3-0 ASP with a rough pass and then he's caught in no man's land #LGRW pic.twitter.com/3hvCAQrNA8 — Red Wings Prospects (@LGRWProspects) September 27, 2026

3-0 ASP with a rough pass and then he's caught in no man's land #LGRW pic.twitter.com/3hvCAQrNA8

Red Wings Prospects (@LGRWProspects) September 27, 2026

"What I can tell you is that on Monday, the roster will go out and you'll see names or whatever," McLellan said. "That could change real quick.

"There can be paper moves; there could be moves made for waiver reasons; there could be something in the hopper somewhere else where you have to buy time."

Larkin and/or Bernard-Docker may be healthy enough to play the opener. Edvinsson might sign a new contract before Friday.

When Larkin is back in the picture, one forward must be dropped. The likely candidate would be Nate Danielson . The Wings could drop Andrew Copp into Danielson's spot, with Larkin taking over as top-line center.

Danielson doesn't have to clear waivers to be assigned to the minors. Carter Mazur would, so by doing it this way, the Wings could buy time to figure out whether Mazur isn't worth risking on the waiver wire.

On defense, when Edvinsson and Bernard-Docker are back, two rearguards must depart. Axel Sandin-Pellikka and Anton Johansson wouldn't require waivers for reassignment. William Wallinder and Englund would.

As much as the Red Wings have liked Anton Johansson's work this preseason, he looked a bit overwhelmed in Saturday's game. Facing a full NHL roster of Columbus Blue Jackets , some warts began to show in Johansson's game.

1-0 Anton has to read this better. Coyle moves to the back post ya gotta box that out or get his stick or stop the pass #LGRW pic.twitter.com/G2Yx23QzPP — Red Wings Prospects (@LGRWProspects) September 26, 2026

1-0 Anton has to read this better. Coyle moves to the back post ya gotta box that out or get his stick or stop the pass #LGRW pic.twitter.com/G2Yx23QzPP

Red Wings Prospects (@LGRWProspects) September 26, 2026

"You could see how for Anton, the game changed a little bit," McLellan said. "There are some bigger, faster, more experienced or intelligent players.

"They know angles better; they know when to jump and when to strip, and so he'll have to get used to that."

What does it all mean? That there are still some tough decisions ahead for the Red Wings.

They may not have to be made by Monday, but judgment day is coming fast for some players.

articles.standfirst: Se trata del torneo profesional de pádel de la Asociación de Jugadores Profesionales de Pádel (AJPP) que se disputaba en el Lawn Tenis Club. Terminó antes de tiempo tras registrarse hechos de violencia y amenazas contra los jugadores Nico Egea y Julián Leite.
articles.summary: Se trata del torneo profesional de pádel de la Asociación de Jugadores Profesionales de Pádel (AJPP) que se disputaba en el Lawn Tenis Club. Terminó antes de tiempo tras registrarse hechos de violencia y amenazas contra los jugadores Nico Egea y Julián Leite.
articles.body: Lo que estaba previsto como una jornada decisiva dentro del calendario profesional de pádel argentino terminó con una suspensión inesperada en La Rioja. El torneo de la Asociación de Jugadores Profesionales de Pádel (AJPP), que se desarrollaba en el Lawn Tenis Club, no pudo completar su programación y tuvo que ser cancelado debido a una serie de incidentes registrados durante la prueba. La situación se produjo después del encuentro correspondiente a los cuartos de final. Según la información difundida y confirmada por los mismos en sus redes, los jugadores Nico Egea y Julián Leite fueron víctimas de agresiones físicas y amenazas por parte de espectadores presentes en el lugar. Frente a este escenario, y ante la preocupación por la seguridad de los deportistas que debían disputar las instancias finales, se decidió no continuar con el certamen. La determinación fue adoptada de común acuerdo entre los jugadores involucrados en las semifinales y la organización después que la propia jueza árbitro tuviera que intervenir y llamar la atención a los jugadores y a la persona que estaba fuera de la pista insultando. El torneo había comenzado el miércoles 23 de septiembre y tenía previsto extenderse hasta el domingo 27. La competencia era además relevante desde el punto de vista deportivo y económico: otorgaba 4.000 puntos para el ranking nacional y contaba con una bolsa de premios de 11 millones de pesos. La AJPP publicó un contundente comunicado lamentando lo sucedido y dejando claro que "la violencia no tiene lugar en el pádel".

articles.title: 6 Tigers Players Who Could Be Gone Before the 2027 Season
articles.summary: The Detroit Tigers face major roster decisions this offseason, with six familiar players potentially gone before the 2027 season begins.
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers entered 2026 expecting to contend for the American League Central.

Detroit enters an important offseason with a young core led by Kevin McGonigle, Max Clark and several other controllable players, but the roster that finished Sunday's season finale won't be the roster that arrives in Lakeland next February.

Some departures are already guaranteed. Others will depend on decisions from president of baseball operations Scott Harris and general manager Jeff Greenberg.

Gleyber Torres and Jack Flaherty are headed for free agency. Three veteran relievers have club options that Detroit must decide whether to exercise. Justin Verlander has already announced his retirement.

That's six recognizable Tigers whose time in Detroit could be over.

And after a disappointing season, there are legitimate reasons to believe the roster could look considerably different in 2027.

Torres may be the most obvious candidate to leave.

The veteran second baseman returned to Detroit after accepting a one-year, $22.025 million qualifying offer last offseason, but injuries prevented him from replicating his All-Star 2025 season.

Torres played 97 games in 2026, batting .260 with eight home runs, 40 RBIs and a .762 OPS.

Detroit also has a potential replacement waiting in Hao-Yu Lee, while the free-agent market could provide other options at second base. The possibility of moving on has already led to the argument that the Tigers should let Torres leave in free agency .

Torres helped Detroit during his two seasons with the organization.

Flaherty's second stint with the Tigers could also be finished.

The right-hander returned from right flexor tendon inflammation to make one final appearance Sunday, allowing one run over two innings.

It may have been his final audition before hitting the open market.

"Taking everything one day at a time," Flaherty said after his final appearance . "Control what you can. Which, for me, is going out and getting ready for next year. Wherever that may be and whenever that may be."

Flaherty struggled through an injury-plagued season and finished with a 5.28 ERA over 21 appearances.

Detroit already has Framber Valdez , Troy Melton , Jackson Jobe and Keider Montero positioned for rotation roles next season.

There could be room for another veteran starter.

It doesn't necessarily have to be Flaherty.

Detroit has a decision to make on its closer.

Jansen's contract contains a $12 million club option for 2027 with a $2 million buyout , meaning the Tigers can move on without paying the full salary.

And there is reason to wonder whether they will.

The veteran right-hander recorded 29 saves in his first season with Detroit, but his year was hardly smooth. Jansen finished with a 4.24 ERA and blew seven save opportunities.

Detroit's bullpen is one of the most obvious areas Harris must address this winter.

In fact, Detroit's offseason outlook identifies finding a new closer as a likely priority.

Jansen is one of the greatest closers in MLB history.

He may have already thrown his final pitch for Detroit.

The Tigers don't just have Jansen's option to consider.

Two other relievers could become free agents depending on what Detroit decides.

Anderson turned himself into one of the more interesting stories on Detroit's pitching staff after returning to Major League Baseball following four seasons in Asia.

He also proved useful in multiple roles.

Anderson started games, pitched out of the bullpen and even handled occasional save situations.

Now Detroit must decide whether that versatility is worth $10 million .

Anderson has a $10 million club option for 2027 with no buyout. Earlier in the season, his strikeout, chase and whiff rates all ranked among the top 20 percent of MLB pitchers .

The Tigers could certainly decide he's worth keeping.

But $10 million is significant money for a pitcher whose primary role isn't guaranteed.

Kinley's decision comes at a considerably lower price.

Detroit holds a $5.5 million option on the veteran reliever for 2027.

The Tigers' bullpen struggled throughout stretches of 2026, and Detroit now has an opportunity to reshape the unit around its younger pitching.

The club must determine whether Kinley fits into that plan or whether the $5.5 million would be better allocated elsewhere.

Together, Jansen, Anderson and Kinley represent $27.5 million in potential 2027 option salaries .

Detroit doesn't have to bring back any of them.

Unlike the other five players, there isn't much suspense here.

Justin Verlander's playing career is over.

The future Hall of Famer announced his retirement earlier this month and made the final start of his career Saturday, ending where everything began more than two decades earlier.

Verlander's return to Detroit gave Tigers fans one final opportunity to watch one of the greatest pitchers in franchise history wear the Old English D.

But his departure also creates another opening on the 2027 pitching staff.

And that brings us back to the larger issue facing Detroit.

This won't simply be an offseason about subtracting players.

Detroit has approximately $85 million committed to its 2027 payroll , giving the organization significant flexibility after opening 2026 with a payroll around $200 million.

The Tigers need more offense. They need bullpen help. They could use another established starting pitcher.

They also need to determine how quickly they are willing to hand larger roles to McGonigle, Clark, Lee and the rest of a young core that became increasingly important as the 2026 season unraveled.

Torres and Flaherty can leave as free agents.

Jansen, Anderson and Kinley could become free agents if Detroit declines their options.

Verlander is already headed into retirement.

And after a 76-win season that fell well short of expectations, don't be surprised if several of them aren't wearing Tigers uniforms when Opening Day arrives in 2027.

articles.title: Italian court convicts three Egyptian agents for kidnap of Giulio Regeni
articles.summary: Defendants were sentenced in absentia to 10 years in prison over the 2016 fatal abduction of the Cambridge scholar.
articles.body:
An Italian court has convicted three Egyptian security officials for their involvement in the kidnapping of student Giulio Regeni, who was later found dead.

The men were sentenced to 10 years in prison for aggravated kidnapping on Monday, while a fourth defendant was acquitted. They were tried in absentia and are unlikely to face extradition given the strained relations between Italy and Egypt as a result of the case.

“We achieved this result despite what can be described as less than wholehearted cooperation from the Egyptian authorities,” Rome Chief Prosecutor Francesco Lo Voi told reporters.

Regeni , a postgraduate student at the United Kingdom’s University of Cambridge, disappeared in the Egyptian capital in January 2016. His body was later found on the side of a road with broken teeth, cigarette burns and broken bones. A post-mortem determined he had been tortured.

Human rights activists said his injuries were similar to those found on people who have been tortured in Egyptian security agency facilities.

Egypt has denied any involvement in his death. The four men, Major Magdi Sharif, from General Intelligence; police Colonel Hisham Helmy; Colonel Ather Kamal, a former head of investigations in Cairo; and former head of state security Major General Tarek Sabir, who was acquitted, have never responded to the accusations against them.

The judge dismissed the accusation of “conspiracy to commit aggravated murder” levelled against Sharif on Monday.

Egyptian and Italian prosecutors initially investigated the case together. However, Egypt then said that members of a criminal gang were responsible for the murder and had been killed in a police shootout. It has subsequently maintained that Regeni’s killers are unknown.

Italian prosecutors said that Egyptian security officials kidnapped and tortured Regeni because of his academic research into trade unions. He had been researching union activities among street vendors in Cairo at the time he disappeared. They accused Egypt of undermining their investigation and refusing to disclose the men’s whereabouts.

Italian legislation allows for the prosecution of crimes ⁠committed abroad against Italian citizens. However, an earlier trial of the four men was suspended in 2021 after the judge questioned its legitimacy, given that the accused may not have known whether they had been charged.

This decision was dismissed in 2023 by Italy’s top court, which said the trial should not be impeded by Egypt’s failure to cooperate. Egypt denied it had refused to cooperate with Italian officials.

articles.body:
Dolphins running back De'Von Achane's season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and the Dolphins made a roster move related to the injury on Monday.

Achane was placed on injured reserve as part of a series of roster moves in Miami . The Dolphins also waived defensive lineman Keith Cooper off of the 53-man roster and released defensive linemen Clelin Ferrell and Jordan Miller from the practice squad.

Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said at a Monday press conference that his "heart breaks" for Achane and said that all of the team's other running backs will have roles in filling in for him.

Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon are the other backs on the 53-man roster, but the Dolphins could add to that group now that they have two open roster spots at their disposal.

articles.title: North Wales Police search for mother after body of baby found in Bangor
articles.summary: The body of the newborn was found near Siliwen Road near the Menai Strait on Sunday.
articles.body:
The body of a newborn baby has been found along a shoreline in north Wales.

North Wales Police has appealed for the mother who may be "extremely vulnerable" to come forward.

A member of the public found the body on the Menai Strait shoreline near Siliwen Road, in Bangor, on Sunday shortly before 17:00 BST.

During a press conference, director of midwifery and women's services for Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board Fiona Giraud has appealed directly to the mother to come forward.

"I want you to know that our immediate concern is for your health, safety and wellbeing. We recognise that you may be feeling frightened, overwhelmed or unsure about what to do next," she said.

The force has not revealed any information about the baby's gender or age.

Giraud said they "have real concerns for the health of the mother".

"We recognise that she is likely to be extremely vulnerable. She may be fearful of seeking the support she needs through fear of identifying herself.

"You may feel you have nowhere to turn, or that you cannot speak to anyone about what has happened. Please do not feel that you have to face this alone.

"We don't yet know all the circumstances surrounding your baby's death but what is important right now is that we find you, make sure you are safe, and ensure you receive any medical attention and support you may need.

"I am asking you personally, to please get in touch with us. You can speak to a healthcare professional, approach a police officer or attend a police station.

"If you are watching or listening to this appeal, please know that we want to hear from you. Please take the first step and contact us. There are people to help you."

Det Sgt Kelly Wynne said they were concerned the mother "may not be in a position to reach out for support", and appealed to the baby's father and the mother's family, friends, neighbours or colleagues who may have information.

"If you have any information regarding a woman or girl you think may have been pregnant or whose behaviour has been unusual or out of character over the past few months including withdrawing from friends, family or social ties, please contact us.

"We appreciate coming forward is difficult, but inaction is not an option."

A post-mortem examination is due to take place on Wednesday afternoon.

The force said people living in Bangor may see an increased police presence over the next few days while the investigation continues.

It urged anyone with information to contact them on 101, quoting Operation Melex.

It added a Major Incident Public Portal (MIPP) had been created where anyone with information that could help the forces enquiries can directly contact police.

articles.title: Major dance festival Terminal V to be held on banks of River Clyde
articles.summary: The event is moving to Glasgow for the first time in 2027, having previously been held in Edinburgh.
articles.body:
Electronic music festival Terminal V will be held on the banks of the River Clyde next year, as the event comes to Glasgow for the first time.

Organisers EE Live announced earlier this year it was moving from Edinburgh to Glasgow for the festival's 10th anniversary in 2027, but did not reveal details of where in the city it would be held.

Now Clydeside Live - a new dedicated open-air event space on the north bank of the river - has been confirmed as the location.

The festival will run from Friday 4 to Sunday 6 June and marks the dance event's first fully outdoor Scottish festival.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

The new venue is intended to be able to host a varied programme of seasonal attractions and entertainment, including gigs, fan zones and sports events.

Organisers Derek Martin and Simon McGrath said the location would let them build the popular festival "from the ground up".

"The scale, the riverside setting and the industrial landscape around it feel completely aligned with Terminal V and give us the freedom to create something we simply couldn't have done before," they said.

"We've seen venues like Silverworks Island [in London] demonstrate just how exciting these large-scale outdoor inner city spaces can be for electronic music, and we believe Clydeside Live has the potential to become one of the most exciting new outdoor event destinations in the UK.

"For our 10th anniversary, we have the opportunity to build the festival from the ground up, rethink our stages and production for the setting and create an experience that feels distinctly Glasgow while still being unmistakably Terminal V."

After launching as a one-day event at Edinburgh's Royal Highland Centre in 2017, Terminal V has expanded to include events in London, Croatia and Australia.

Organisers say more than 30% of ticket sales come from outside Scotland and that previous editions have contributed more than £5m to the local economy.
