articles.title: India's League of Legends team returns to Asian Games with Hangzhou lessons
articles.summary: At 24, Akshaj Shenoy is heading back to the Asian Games as captain of India's League of Legends team.
articles.body: At 24, Akshaj Shenoy is heading back to the Asian Games as captain of India's League of Legends team. But becoming a professional player was never part of the original plan.He started playing for fun. Then came the tournaments, better opponents and more time spent understanding the competitive side of the game. There was no single moment when he decided esports would become a profession.“It happened gradually as I got better opportunities and started seeing how far I could take it,” Shenoy told Timesofindia.com.By the time India reached the Asian Games in Hangzhou, Shenoy was studying Economics, Sociology and Industrial Relations while playing professionally and coordinating practice with teammates based in different cities.Three years on, he is returning as the captain and four of the six players who will represent India in League of Legends at Aichi-Nagoya were part of the Hangzhou campaign, where India finished fifth. Ahmed Shahid and Rahul Bisht are the two newcomers.“We look back at Hangzhou with a lot of pride, but also knowing that we could have gone further,” Shenoy said. “Once you've experienced that stage and seen that you can compete with some of the best teams in Asia, you naturally feel that there's more you can achieve.”A game that demands five players to think as oneLeague of Legends is a 5v5 team-based strategy game in which players control unique characters, known as champions, and work together to destroy the opposing team’s Nexus, the central structure in their base. Each team has five roles, namely Top, Jungle, Mid, ADC and Support, with each serving a different function. Players have different roles and responsibilities, but at the professional level, communication and decision-making are as important as individual skill.“You're constantly thinking about where the opponents could be, what they might do next and how you should respond,” Shenoy said. “At the same time, you're managing your own resources, positioning, timing and trying to make decisions based on what your teammates are doing.”The game was launched in 2009 and has grown into one of the world's major esports titles, with professional competitions across regions and an annual World Championship.For India, however, the challenge is less about finding people who play the game and more about creating enough high-level competition for players to develop against. Shenoy has seen that difference first-hand.The group that stayed togetherAfter Hangzhou, some of the Indian players continued competing together in domestic and South Asian League of Legends tournaments. They played more tournaments, won titles and spent more time as a unit. That continuity also gave them a better understanding of how each player communicates and reacts in different situations.S8UL signed the group in 2025, giving the players a more structured environment around training and competition.For S8UL co-founder and CEO Animesh Agarwal, that continuity is one of the roster's biggest strengths. He said the players had spent years “playing together, adapting to different competitive environments and developing a strong understanding of each other's game”.The roster won Legends Ascend South Asia in 2025 and later competed in the LCP Promotion Wild Card Playoffs, finishing fifth.“Playing against stronger regional teams gave us valuable experience and showed us where we still needed to improve,” Shenoy said.Six players, six different routesShenoy is the most obvious link between the two Asian Games campaigns.The Kochi-based 24-year-old was part of India's Hangzhou team and his esports career has run alongside education and work. Before Hangzhou, he was studying three subjects while playing professionally and coordinating practice sessions for teammates based in different cities. His parents, he said, were supportive of his choices.Today, he is preparing for an MBA and helps with his father's business.Back home, much of his day goes into studying and working on the business. Around 8 pm, he gets online with his teammates, with practice often continuing until 1 am because everyone has different studies and jobs to work around.“I've always enjoyed gaming and, more importantly, the competitive side of esports, so it remains a big part of my life,” he said.Mihir Ranjan is an IIM Ahmedabad graduate based in Delhi. Aakash Shandilya is from Noida and works as a cloud engineering intern. Sanindhya Malik is based in Mauritius and works with Telecommunications Consultants India Ltd.Ahmed Shahid, a Chemical Engineering graduate from Aligarh, and 29-year-old Rahul Bisht, a product designer and entrepreneur from Bengaluru, are making their Asian Games debuts.The six players arrive at Aichi-Nagoya with very different lives outside the game. For most of them, esports has had to fit around education, jobs and other responsibilities rather than replace them.What Hangzhou left behindThe first Asian Games appearance gave Shenoy a different understanding of what it meant to play for India. “What I remember most is walking out there and realising that we were representing India on such a huge stage,” Shenoy said. “There was a lot of pride, but also a sense of responsibility that came with wearing the India jersey.”The experience also showed the players what was required to compete against Asia's strongest teams. “We've had a few years since then to grow together, compete at a higher level and understand what it takes to perform on a stage like this,” he said.The four returning players know what the stage feels like. Ahmed has been around the group for a long time despite making his Asian Games debut, while Rahul has adapted quickly during the preparations, according to Shenoy.“At the end of the day, we trust each other, and my job is to make sure everyone feels comfortable enough to play their own game when the pressure is at its highest.”The gap India is still trying to closeShenoy has also seen India's esports environment become more organised since Hangzhou, with more tournaments, organisations and opportunities for players. But he believes the gap with the leading League of Legends regions remains clear.“The biggest difference is probably the amount of regular high-level competition and the depth of the player pool,” Shenoy said.In Korea, China and Vietnam, players are surrounded by strong competition and have more opportunities to test themselves against high-level opposition.Indian players have had to be more proactive in finding those opportunities. “In India, we've had to be more proactive about finding those opportunities and learning from every international event we get to play,” Shenoy said.Playing together consistently has helped the group develop its communication and understanding, while S8UL has provided a more professional environment around the team.Joining the organisation, Shenoy said, gave the players more support with training and preparation and the confidence to look beyond India. “It also gave us more confidence to look beyond the Indian ecosystem and take international competition seriously,” he said.But he sees a longer-term requirement for the game in India.“There are more organisations, tournaments and opportunities for players to build a career,” Shenoy said. “At the same time, League of Legends still needs a deeper player pool and more regular high-level competition in India.”For the next generation, he wants clearer pathways into competitive play. “The interest and talent are definitely there. The next step is building an ecosystem that can sustain that talent over the long term.”South Korea, Chinese Taipei and Hong Kong awaitIndia has been drawn alongside South Korea (2022 Asian Games Gold Medallist), Chinese Taipei (2022 Asian Games Silver Medallist) and Hong Kong in Group B at Aichi-Nagoya. For Shenoy, the group offers a direct measure of how much Indian League of Legends has developed.The established Asian regions have deeper player pools and more regular high-level competition. Playing against them means testing how quickly the Indian players can make decisions, adapt and respond under pressure, but India is not travelling simply to observe.“We don't want to go in thinking we're simply there to learn,” Shenoy said. “We've prepared seriously and we want to compete.”“What they see on stage is the result of years of work behind the scenes,” he said. “There are countless hours of practice, travelling, studying the game and balancing esports with education, jobs and life outside gaming.”“For us, wearing the India jersey is something we've worked towards for a long time. It's a huge responsibility, but it's also a privilege.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Rockstar Games has revealed new details about the weather system in GTA 6, confirming that players will experience hurricanes, tropical storms, heavy rain, and strong winds in Leonida. The game will also feature changing weather, with rain falling in one area while the sun shines in another. According to a new report from Game Informer, Rockstar has improved its weather system to make the world feel more real. The updated system will also bring lasting puddles, moving clouds, lightning, and realistic wind effects.GTA 6 to bring hurricanes, tropical storms, and changing weather to LeonidaRockstar’s latest weather reveal shows how the studio plans to bring Florida-like weather to Leonida, the fictional state where GTA 6 takes place. Speaking to Game Informer, Owen Shepherd, Rockstar’s vice president of art for lighting and rendering, explained that the team had rebuilt its weather system.“We have re-engineered our weather system to make everything much more localized and persistent, and really wanted the world to feel dynamically solid and achieve a sense of scale we haven’t felt before,” Shepherd said.This means players may see storms moving across the map, with heavy rain affecting one area while another stays sunny. The game will also have large storm clouds, lightning, and changing skies.Rain will leave marks on the world even after it stops. Puddles will remain on roads and other surfaces, showing where rain has fallen. Players may also see rainbows when the sunlight and weather conditions are right.Rockstar is also adding hurricanes and tropical storms, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, thunder, and lightning to Leonida. Water will pour from rooftops and streetlights during these powerful storms.GTA 6 weather system to feature realistic wind, rain, and environmental effectsThe new weather system will also change how wind affects the game world. Rockstar is adding different wind patterns, including sea breezes after sunset and warm air rising during the day. Buildings will also block and change the direction of the wind.Shepherd explained how these effects will appear in the game. “Hair and debris will swirl around on roof-tops; gusts of wind will blow ripples over the water surface and bend the grass in swamps,” he said.These details could make Leonida feel more alive as players explore its cities, beaches, and swamps. The weather will not simply change the sky, but will also affect objects and the environment around players.The latest reveal follows years of rumors about GTA 6’s advanced weather system. articles.title: Chicago Cubs quickly KO’d from playoffs after bats quiet again in 4-1 loss to San Diego Padres
articles.summary: SAN DIEGO — Major League Baseball’s best offense in the regular season will be watching the rest of the playoffs from home. After a season defined by extreme...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO — Major League Baseball's best offense in the regular season will be watching the rest of the playoffs from home.

After a season defined by extreme highs and lows, the Chicago Cubs played from behind in all but one inning and were swept in a National League wild-card series against the San Diego Padres with a 4-1 loss Wednesday night.

Four Cubs pitchers — Kevin Gausman , Daniel Palencia , David Peterson and Ryan Zeferjahn — kept the Padres in check enough to give the offense a chance. This team was built around offense and defense, and the bats never came alive in a disappointing performance. The group underwhelmed, managing just one run and nine hits over the 18 innings in the series.

Their offensive futility started at the top with the Cubs' best two hitters. Pete Crow-Armstrong , looking to deliver a better postseason performance than a year ago, and Alex Bregman , playing despite multiple facial fractures, combined to go 0-for-15 with eight strikeouts and one walk in the two games.

The depth of the lineup, a strength in the regular season, yielded little. Only four players had a hit in the two-game sweep: Nico Hoerner (four), Seiya Suzuki (two), Tyrone Taylor (one) and Carson Kelly (one). Hoerner's one-out double in the ninth Wednesday represented their only extra-base hit of the series.

The woes at the plate became a recipe for postseason disaster.

Hoerner's single up the middle in the fourth produced the Cubs' lone wild-card run. Dansby Swanson had a particularly rough night at the plate. Twice he was at the center of wasted scoring opportunities. With two on and nobody out in the third against Padres starter Nick Pivetta , Swanson worked a 3-0 count before striking out on a fastball near his ankles. Crow-Armstrong then popped out and Bregman flied out to end the inning.

The big moment found Swanson again the following inning. Padres reliever Bradgley Rodríguez hit Kelly to load the bases, but Swanson flied out on the first pitch from the right-hander off a 99.3-mph fastball up and in.

The Cubs finished 1-for-6 with runners in scoring position in the loss and left six runners on base.

Gavin Sheets ' pinch-hit two-run home run off Palencia, with the Padres faithful chanting "Holy Sheets!" as the at-bat began, provided the big blow in the fourth inning minutes after Hoerner pulled the Cubs within a run.

For a team that touted its veteran experience all year, especially heading into the postseason, the Cubs ultimately failed to rise to the moment. They will be left to wonder if the series would have played out differently had they not squandered home-field advantage in the final week of the regular season after going 4-1 at Wrigley Field during the 2025 playoffs.

The elimination situation is a position Craig Counsell was familiar with as Wednesday represented his 20th postseason game as a manager.

"The back's against the wall," Counsell said before Game 2. "It's a real thing, and it's a great place to be. I think some people might not like it. I think athletes love it. Put my back against the wall, and I've got to fight. I've got to fight or it's over. That's a good place to be."

The Cubs, though, never seemed to settle in during the series. The majors' top run-scoring offense and leader in home runs didn't put much pressure on the Padres.

One of the better teams with their hitters' usage of the ABS system in the regular season, the Cubs weren't as judicious on a night when the slimmest of margins could determine whether their season ended or continued. Crow-Armstrong challenged a strike-three call to lead off the first inning that replay showed nearly half the ball inside the zone. Then the Cubs lost their second challenge when Kelly tapped his helmet from behind the plate for a review with nobody on in the third for a would-be 3-2 count to Fernando Tatís Jr.

The Cubs head into an offseason full of uncertainty. Beyond the looming lockout, the Cubs have questions to solve, particularly surrounding a pitching staff that was decimated by injuries and how to build a roster that can go deeper in the playoffs after falling short of expectations two consecutive years.

articles.summary: O abastecimento de água em Barra Mansa foi normalizado no bairro Verbo Divino, mas equipes seguem em obras na cratera da Rua Major Eduardo Pereira da Costa Rangel.
articles.body:
Abastecimento de água é restabelecido no bairro Verbo Divino em Barra Mansa. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barra Mansa

O abastecimento de água foi restabelecido nesta sexta-feira (2) no bairro Verbo Divino, em Barra Mansa (RJ). Equipes da prefeitura trabalham na recuperação da rede de drenagem e da rua Major Eduardo Pereira da Costa Rangel, onde uma cratera se abriu após o forte volume de chuva registrado na quarta-feira (30).

Segundo a prefeitura, o rompimento da antiga tubulação de drenagem provocou o afundamento do asfalto. A rua permanece interditada no trecho em obras, e o trânsito precisou ser alterado para garantir a segurança de moradores e trabalhadores.

De acordo com o Serviço Autônomo de Água e Esgoto (Saae), as equipes realizam um reforço na estrutura da rede para manter o abastecimento durante as obras. O trabalho também considera a previsão de chuva e a possibilidade de instabilidade do solo durante o fim de semana.

As equipes realizam uma substituição do trecho danificado da tubulação e na recomposição da área. Somente após essa etapa, poderá ser realizado a recuperação do pavimento.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil de Barra Mansa, os agentes continuam monitorando as condições meteorológicas e os locais que registraram ocorrências provocadas pelas chuvas.

O órgão acompanha a situação em conjunto com o Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden) e orienta a população a acompanhar os alertas oficiais e evitar áreas com risco de alagamentos, deslizamentos ou quedas de árvores.

Em caso de emergência, a Defesa Civil pode ser acionada pelo telefone 199 ou pelo WhatsApp (24) 98121-3427. O Corpo de Bombeiros atende pelo 193.

articles.title: Widdecombe suspect charged with planning acts of terror against Farage
articles.summary: Counter terror police say the further charge comes after a "hugely intensive and complex investigation".
articles.body:
The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe has also been charged with preparing acts of terror including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Counter terror police said Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged on Friday with one count of preparation of terrorist acts.

The charge relates to activity which is alleged to have taken place between May 2024 and July 2026.

Kerry was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman.

Counter Terrorism Policing Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said the charge on Friday was the result of a "hugely intensive and complex investigation".

"This investigation has been led by a dedicated team of detectives, analysts, and forensic experts, working on multiple lines of enquiry, which has resulted in this very serious charge," she added.

Kerry, from Rotherham, is due to appear in court over the terror charge on Wednesday, police said.

Frank Ferguson of the Crown Prosecution Service's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division said prosecutors "worked closely" with police to bring the charge and would continue to work alongside them as the investigation continued.

Widdecombe was found dead on Thursday 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

She served as Conservative MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

Following her departure from the Commons, Widdecombe appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing and would later become a Reform UK spokeswoman.

articles.title: Former Blue Jays Catcher Ali Sánchez Joins Yankees For ALDS
articles.summary: While the Toronto Blue Jays season ended, former catcher Ali Sánchez is now active on the New York Yankees roster for the ALDS in a surprising twist.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays season ended in disappointment, yet one of their former catchers is now playing for their biggest rival in the playoffs. Ali Sánchez, who wore number 20 for Toronto, is currently on the New York Yankees' active roster for the American League Division Series. This switch happened just as the Jays were officially knocked out of contention. "One year after coming within 90 feet of winning the World Series, the Toronto Blue Jays' season is over. They are officially eliminated from postseason play," Bob Nightengale reported for USA Today. It is a stark contrast to see a former member of that group helping the Yankees chase a title just days later.

Sánchez did not start the season with the Bronx Bombers. He spent time with Toronto and even Boston before finding his way to New York. The Yankees signed him to a Major League contract right before a game on June 6, according to the New York Yankees official release. "Prior to tonight's game, the Yankees signed C Ali Sánchez (#39) to a Major League contract and," the team stated in their announcement. He quickly earned a spot on the 26-man roster for the ALDS. The team posted on social media, "Our 26 for the ALDS. #RepBX | #Postseason." This move shows how quickly a player can go from being a bench option to a playoff contributor.

Sánchez brings a specific skill set that fits the Yankees' current needs. His 51-game 2026 regular season ended with a .244 batting average, 21 hits, one home run, eight RBIs, and seven runs. While the numbers are modest, his presence adds depth behind the plate. The switch from wearing number 20 in Toronto to number 39 in New York marks a complete change of scenery.

Teams often look for players who have seen the league from different angles. Sánchez has played for multiple organizations, including the Blue Jays and Red Sox, before landing in the Bronx. "The athletic 29-year-old is no stranger to a baffling blunder, but he's also extremely talented and younger than most free agents," a former scout noted about his profile. This mix of youth and experience makes him a valuable asset during a long playoff run. He was previously signed to a minor league deal by Toronto before moving on to other teams.

The timing of his arrival could not be better for the Yankees. With the postseason underway, having a fresh catcher who knows the league well is a huge boost. The team needs every hand they can get to navigate the tough competition ahead. Sánchez's journey from a minor league signing to a playoff roster spot is a testament to his persistence. He had to clear waivers and sign multiple contracts to get here, but he made it work. "Boston Red Sox claimed C Ali Sánchez off waivers from Toronto Blue Jays," which was a key step in his path to New York.

Now he faces the team he left behind in spirit, if not in uniform. The Yankees hope his fresh legs and sharp mind will help them secure a win. As the series moves forward, every play behind the plate matters. Sánchez has a chance to make his mark on the biggest stage. The goal is simple: help the team win. "be in a similar area of support" was a phrase used regarding his role, suggesting he provides stability where needed. The Yankees are looking for that exact kind of steady hand as they push for the next round.

articles.body: LUCKNOW: Four people, including the only son, brother and nephew of a deceased Army officer, were killed when the ambulance carrying his body from Panchkula to Deoria rammed into a stationary truck on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur district on Sunday morning.The deceased were identified as Gaurav Singh (18), the only son of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh; Ram Samujh (55), the soldier’s brother; Rajan Singh (35), his nephew and relative; and ambulance driver Jaspal.The accident occurred around 8.15am near Haliyapur on the Ayodhya-Sultanpur border, around kilometre marker 79.6 of the expressway.According to police, the ambulance was travelling from Panchkula to Deoria carrying the mortal remains of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh when it crashed into a truck parked on the roadside. The impact was so severe that the front portion of the ambulance was completely mangled.Gaurav and driver Jaspal, who were seated in the front, died on the spot. The driver’s body became trapped inside the wreckage and had to be extricated by cutting open the vehicle with a gas cutter.The other two passengers, Ram Samujh and Rajan Singh, were rushed to a government hospital in Ayodhya. Both succumbed to their injuries during treatment.Family was returning with soldier’s mortal remainsPolice said Subedar Major Satyawan Singh, a resident of Rudrapur in Deoria, was serving in the Army and had been posted in Meerut. He had been undergoing treatment at the Command Hospital in Chandigarh and had undergone a kidney transplant.He died in Panchkula three days before the accident.After his death, his brother Ram Samujh, nephew Rajan Singh and son Gaurav travelled to Panchkula to bring his body back to the family’s native place in Deoria.The three relatives left Panchkula around 4pm on Saturday in the ambulance, while other family members followed them in another vehicle.At around 8.15am on Sunday, the ambulance crashed into the stationary truck near Haliyapur.Police suspect driver may have dozed offAccording to police, a preliminary investigation suggests that the accident may have occurred after the ambulance driver possibly fell asleep at the wheel. Witnesses also told police that the ambulance appeared to be travelling at high speed before it suddenly went out of control and crashed into the truck.Police teams reached the spot after receiving information from passers-by and Dial 112. The bodies were taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination.Officials are also examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area to establish the exact sequence of events.Sultanpur District Magistrate Indrajeet Singh said the deceased Army officer had been undergoing treatment at the Command Hospital in Chandigarh and had undergone a kidney transplant. He confirmed that three members of the soldier’s family and the ambulance driver died in the accident.Sultanpur Superintendent of Police Vineet Jaiswal said police received information about the accident through Dial 112 and immediately deployed a local police team to the spot. articles.title: Miami Heat Continues Its Wait for Its Last Roster Spot While Free Agents Bounce Around
articles.summary: Training camp has started, but the Miami Heat have yet to find the perfect candidate for their last open roster spot. The team still needs one more guard and...
articles.body:
Training camp has started, but the Miami Heat have yet to find the perfect candidate for their last open roster spot. The team still needs one more guard and had a variety of options in front of them, including multiple free agents: Gabe Vincent , Ryan Nembhard , and even D'Angelo Russell before his sudden career move .

Miami Heat Continues Its Wait to Fill Last Roster Spot

But despite having cap space to make a veteran minimum-salary deal, there is no movement from Miami's side suggesting they are looking for someone.

Russell and Vincent have been linked to the Heat since the beginning of this off-season, while Nembhard has been linked more recently. But there have been certain issues attached to everyone holding back Miami.

Vincent, who was traded to the Atlanta Hawks in February, has been on the open market for a while now. In Miami, he has been a preferred candidate for Bam Adebayo , who has shared the court with him in the past and wants him on the current roster. However, despite internal interest and strong link-up rumors, Miami hasn't made a move for him. His health is an issue.

Vincent could also find refuge with the New York Knicks despite recently rejecting their camp offer. As for Nembhard, who the Charlotte Hornets waived on September 26, he signed a two-way deal with the Denver Nuggets on September 30.

Missed Opportunity With D'Angelo Russell

Russell was receiving significant media attention as a potential target for Miami throughout the offseason. He would have fulfilled their playmaking depth and backcourt needs, but despite strong rumors, this never materialized. Russell's chances with Miami are over for now, as he recently left the NBA to continue his professional career in the Chinese Basketball Association, joining the Shanghai Sharks .

This year, Russell was traded twice before being waived toward the end of last month. Russell was moved from the Dallas Mavericks to the Washington Wizards in February, and then to the Memphis Grizzlies in July. However, Memphis waived him last week, giving Miami the perfect opportunity to lock him down if they wanted.

But his recent health issues could be a roadblock in their path, as this season Miami only wants healthy, available players. And now that window is closed, and the 30-year-old is heading to China for the next season.

According to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald , the Heat are "expected to be patient with its 15th roster spot," which will allow them to observe and make a sound decision by choosing someone who they see as a "real difference-maker." And beyond the free agents, a buyout is another method to achieve this goal.

Currently, the Heat have 14 players on standard contracts, including 13 veterans and one rookie, and all three two-way spots filled. Continuing from last season are: Bam Adebayo , Andrew Wiggins , Nikola Jović , Davion Mitchell , Pelle Larsson , Simone Fontecchio , Dru Smith , Myron Gardner , while added this year are: Giannis Antetokounmpo , Bobby Portis , Tim Hardaway Jr., Klay Thompson , Nick Richards , Tre Donaldson (2-way deal), and Ryan Conwell .

As Miami continues to hesitate in making a choice, there is also the idea on the back burner that they might enter the season with 14 players while buying time for the last piece of the puzzle. But lately, Miami has been holding off on some important decisions, only to finalize them at the last minute, like extending Larsson on a 4-year contract recently.

If they make up their minds, they can surprise everyone with a last-minute signing before the official season starts.

articles.title: De ganar un torneo amateur y dejar su trabajo como fisio a ir al Mundial con Francia: el salto al vacío de Clara Mansart
articles.standfirst: La joven jugadora francesa en octubre de 2025 jugó en Milán una competición que le llevaría a saltar al circuito FIP Tour y, ahora, a ser convocada para Doha.
articles.summary: La joven jugadora francesa en octubre de 2025 jugó en Milán una competición que le llevaría a saltar al circuito FIP Tour y, ahora, a ser convocada para Doha.
articles.body: Hay giros de guion en el deporte que superan cualquier ficción, historias donde el esfuerzo silencioso y la pasión transforman una vida en cuestión de meses. Y un buen ejemplo es el que ha experimentado Clara Mansart (2001, Francia) que en apenas un año ha pasado de proclamarse campeona de un torneo amateur a ser convocada por primera vez con Francia para el Mundial de Doha (Catar). Una historia que tiene su primer punto de inflexión a principios de octubre de 2025 cuando Mansart, tras superar las fases locales de la competición amateur Oysho Padel Cup en suelo francés, se clasificó a la fase final para el torneo de Milán coincidiendo con el P1 de Premier Padel. Una oportunidad que le daría a diferentes jugadoras amateur la posibilidad de jugar en la pista central del Allianz Cloud y lo que podía haber sido una simple experiencia, se acabaría convirtiendo en el inicio de algo más. "Para mí, la Oysho Pádel Cup fue un torneo muy importante porque tuve la oportunidad de jugar en la pista central del P1 de Milán y poder vivir ese tipo de experiencia me hizo querer vivir más grandes citas internacionales", rememora con nostalgia la jugadora gala de lo que sin saber sería un cambio vital. Porque como en toda buena historia de película, un pequeño gesto sería el desencadenante del gran cambio. Inesperado y sutil, lo que días atrás era un sueño se iba a convertir en un “y si…” que acabaría siendo. “Ese torneo reforzó todavía más mi pasión por el pádel y me hizo pensar en hasta dónde podía llegar si realmente me dedicaba al cien por cien a este deporte. Y así empecé a jugar el circuito FIP”, explica sobre cómo tomó la decisión de empezar su carrera profesional. Aquel flechazo con las grandes citas encendió un fuego interior que ya no volvería a apagarse. Mansart, que creció empuñando una raqueta de tenis a los cuatro años tras una recomendación materna para alejarla del fútbol que jugaba su padre, halló en la pala esa chispa que creía olvidada. “Con el tiempo, sentía que el tenis ya no me aportaba las mismas sensaciones y que necesitaba un nuevo desafío. El pádel me permitió recuperar esa ilusión y esas ganas de descubrir hasta dónde podía llegar”, confiesa. Tras un par de años compaginando ambas disciplinas, el veneno del pádel, esa adicción que todo el que lo prueba conoce, terminó por atraparla a los 22 años. La disciplina y exigencia de la élite adquiridas en la pista le sirvieron como catapulta para una rápida adaptación que supo suplir con creces al no haber vivido la formación en categorías inferiores. Pero, ¿cómo llega la decisión definitiva? Hace apenas unos meses, en verano de 2026, Clara decidiría traducir su hambre competitiva en una decisión determinante: pausar su vida, dejar en standby su carrera como fisioterapeuta para volcarse en el pádel y comenzar a entrenar en una academia profesional en París. Una apuesta de riesgo pues, aún lejos de la élite, la vida de la jugadora que aspira a ser profesional es sacrificada y con muchos riesgos económicos. “Todavía no vivo del pádel. He podido ahorrar algo de dinero, pero jugar el circuito FIP supone muchos gastos: desplazamientos, hoteles, vuelos, trenes… todo suma muy rápido”, detalla con sinceridad sobre el día a día de la competición. Partido a partido, viaje a viaje, torneo a torneo, Mansart ya está inmersa en el top-10 del ranking femenino en Francia y ha conseguido escalar hasta la plaza 173 del ranking FIP. Una realidad donde premios y patrocinadores buscan conseguir ese frágil equilibrio que le dé sentido a todo. “No hago esto para ganarme la vida con el pádel, sino para poder vivir del deporte que me apasiona. Es por viajar, competir, rendir al máximo y alcanzar mis objetivos deportivos, pero está claro que este proyecto tendrá un límite en el tiempo si no consigo suficiente apoyo”, narra sobre la cara B del camino a la élite. Una historia que le ha llevado, en apenas unos meses, de vivir sus primeras ilusiones en un circuito amateur a compartir vestuario con referentes del pádel mundial como Alix Collombon o Léa Godallier. Un salto, y qué salto, que dibuja a la perfección la magia del deporte de la pala y premia la valentía de quien decidió apostarlo todo por un sueño. Así se daría la llamada de la selección, en medio de un camino abnegado, de maletas preparadas a toda prisa y cuentas al milímetro. Y al otro lado de la línea Juan Alday, el seleccionador de Francia, que le confirmaba su convocatoria para representar a la selección absoluta en el Mundial de Doha. “Me puse súper feliz y también muy emocionada cuando me llamó el seleccionador. Ser seleccionada para representar a mi país es una de las recompensas más bonitas por todo el trabajo que he realizado durante estos últimos años”, recuerda con una emoción de esas que el rostro, involuntariamente, no puede esconder. Para Clara ponerse la camiseta bleu representa la cúspide de un viaje que lejos de ser solitario ha sido compartido. "Evidentemente pensé en todas las personas que me han acompañado desde el principio. Siento que esta selección también es una recompensa para ellas porque sin su apoyo no habría llegado hasta aquí", reconoce dando razón a aquellos que dicen que si quieres llegar lejos siempre es mejor viajar acompañado. Una trama que podría haber sido otro inspirador documental más del catálogo de Netflix, pero que nada tiene de ficción, es la historia real de una persona con nombres y apellidos que soñó tan fuerte que se convirtió en jugadora profesional de pádel. “Es realmente un sueño que se hace realidad. Ahora tengo muchas ganas de darlo todo y representar a Francia de la mejor manera posible”, finaliza ilusionada esta joven jugadora francesa. El viaje que arrancó en la moqueta amateur del Allianz Cloud ya ha tenido varias paradas y escalas en forma de torneos, países, victorias y derrotas en apenas unos meses y en pocos días vivirá un nuevo e ilusionante destino representando a Francia en el Mundial. Y si lo encara con la misma humildad y hambre con la que arrancó esta aventura, quizá Milán no era el final del camino, eran tan solo el principio.

articles.title: Joshua Kerry accused of trying to break into Nigel Farage's home
articles.summary: Joshua Kerry, 28, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court and was remanded in custody.
articles.body:
The man accused of murdering the former MP Ann Widdecombe in July has appeared in court faced with a new allegation of preparing terrorist acts, including trying to break into the home of Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Prosecutor Kashif Malik said Joshua Kerry, 28, is alleged to have carried out online reconnaissance of "prominent people and institutions... including identifying the home address of Nigel Farage".

The prosecutor later told Westminster Magistrates' Court that damage was found on the doorframe at Farage's home address, adding: "the inference is that an attempt was made to gain entry to the house".

Kerry was accompanied by four custody officers in the dock and was remanded in custody to appear at the Old Bailey on Friday.

Kerry appeared in person the court. With a thick beard and wearing a grey sweatshirt and trousers, he spoke only to confirm his address in Rotherham and his date of birth.

He was told he faced a new charge of preparing terrorist acts between 31 May 2024 and 8 July 2026 by carrying out research on targets and travelling to, and attempting to gain entry to, the home of Nigel Farage.

The court heard that in April 2025 Nigel Farage's partner found that damage had been caused to their main front door at their house and a bottle of lighter fluid was found in the porch.

Kerry was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman.

Widdecombe was found dead on 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

She served as Conservative MP for Maidstone and the Weald in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s. She became a member of Reform UK in 2019.

articles.title: 49ers-Seahawks: 3 major differences from last year’s roster
articles.summary: The 49ers overhauled their roster at wide receiver, plus they have some key pieces returning who didn’t play late against the Seahawks last season
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers faced the Seattle Seahawks three times in 2025. Kyle Shanahan's offense had 30 drives against Mike MacDonald's defense. They scored two touchdowns.

In the first matchup, Ricky Pearsall had over 100 receiving yards, while Zach Charbonnet led Seattle in rushing. Neither player will be in uniform this Sunday.

In the second matchup, the 49ers' leading receiver was Jauan Jennings. Cornerback Riq Woolen had a pass breakup. Those two are on different teams.

In the playoff matchup, Kenneth Walker ran for 116 yards, while Jake Tonges had a team-high in receiving for the Niners. Walker is with the Chiefs, while Tonges is on the injured reserve.

Even in that Week 1 matchup, 45 of Pearsall's 108 yards came on one play. Christian McCaffrey and Kyle Juszczyk each had 25-yard receptions. For the most part, the passing attack was held in check because, as they showed in the next two games, no wideout could consistently get open.

Mike Evans is seventh in the NFL in EPA per target and fifth in targeted success percentage. He's what a true WR1 looks like. The only reason he's seventh in Sumer Sports' impact plays metric is because he's only been targeted 24 times. For reference, the six receivers ahead of Evans have at least 39 targets.

Kyle Shanahan moves Evans around the formation enough that defenses can't key in on him. That has led to incredible efficiency. Of Evans' 17 receptions, 14 have resulted in either a first down or a touchdown.

The struggles against Seattle are why you go out and get a receiver of Evans' caliber.

In Week 18, the 49ers wide receivers were Jauan Jennings, Kendrick Bourne, Demarcus Robinson, and Skyy Moore. It's a completely different group this time around.

There's speed around Evans, which has opened things up and allowed the 49ers to stretch the field both vertically and horizontally. Evans isn't catching intermediate passes with Bourne or Jennings on the field, because teams like Seattle aren't threatened deep.

Brock Purdy will also have George Kittle and Deebo Samuel, two players who weren't available in the playoffs.

In those final two matchups, the 49ers started two players who had signed to the roster as recently as Thanksgiving, plus Dee Winters. The fact that the Niners were so eager to move on from Winters this offseason, despite his rookie contract, tells us how they felt about him internally. Raheem Morris views Garret Wallow as a nickel linebacker, while Kendricks is 34.

There were plays where Seattle ran to the outside, and Kendricks, understandably, was a step slow. Wallow would get swallowed up, while Winters' best work came on plays right at him or in coverage.

Quietly, the 49ers have been one of the best teams at defending outside zone — the Seahawks run some variation outside of the tackles 60% of the time. The Niners have allowed 3.7 yards per play on outside zone runs, with a -0.045 EPA per play. On 16 attempts, they've had nine defensive stops.

It's been a mix-and-match of players on the edge. They've done their jobs, but Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw are winning the foot race when running backs try to beat them to the sideline.

In Week 18, Tatum Bethune and Winters combined for three missed tackles. Seattle torched Bethune in coverage, to the tune of 64 yards. Bethune allowed six of his seven targets to be completed. Wallow got lost on one play in coverage, leading to a critical first down.

It goes without saying that Warner will impact where Sam Darnold throws the ball. If he targets Warner seven times, Raheem Morris will take that all day. The upgrade at linebacker cannot be undersold heading into this matchup.

Yetur Gross-Matos was the only player to generate interior pressure against the Seahawks during the regular season. In those three games, five defensive tackles recorded seven run stops and five missed tackles.

Let's look at the past two games this season, since those are the defensive tackles who will play this week for the 49ers. Osa Odighizuwa has eight pressures. Gracen Halton and Sebastian Valdez have five impact plays. Naquan Jones has a couple of run stops and is holding his ground.

The four defensive tackles on the field this year are all upgrades from last year.

One of the most impressive areas from Week 3 was seeing the edge players play the run. Matt Judon played one snap, and it looked great. Romello Height is wiry strong, while Keion White has been a pleasant surprise.

The edge presence who didn't play in the final two games is Mykel Williams. The 49ers' run defense allowed a half-yard-per-play more with Mykel off the field last season. The first-down rate and EPA per play were marginally better.

What you can't quantify is having a player his size going up against tight ends. Those are wins for Williams. Or having Mykel take on pulling blockers instead of your designated pass rushers, like Height.

Even if Williams plays only 30 snaps, you get to keep Height, Okoronkwo, and Khalid Kareem fresh. The domino effect of getting a first-rounder back has immense benefits for the Niners' defense.
